title: The Implementation of Infant Anoesis and Adult Autonoesis in the Retrogenesis and Staging System of the Neurocognitive Disorders: A Proposal for a Multidimensional Person-Centered Model
content:
BACKGROUND. Retrogenesis is the process by which the degenerative and vascular mechanisms of dementias reverse the order of acquisition in the normal development. 
OBJECTIVE. The development of memory/knowledge after birth may help to know the biopsychosocial and functional characteristics (biosphere) of the retrogenesis.
METHODS. A literature review was performed by consulting the PubMed, Google Scholar and Scopus databases. The research was conducted using 43 keywords related to retrogenesis: a total of 234 eligible records were selected.
RESULTS. The infantile amnesia was described taking in account the infant child biosphere in which the limbic system progressively develops the acquisition of the body knowledge (Anoetic Body Consciousness-AnBC) until the age of 3-4 years. At this age usually the AnBC evolves as a continuum into the adulthood autonoesis with the emergence in the child-adolescent of the Episodic Autobiographic Memory (EAM) and the development of Autonoetic Mind Consciousness (AuMC). The development of cognition and knowledge from birth to adulthood is due to the progressive maturation of the whole limbic system and not only of the hippocampus. In the biopsychosocial retrogenesis, the EAM/AuMC vanishes progressively along the mild, moderate and severe stages of dementias when the infant AnBC resurfaces losing progressively the basic Activities of Daily Living in a retrogenetic order of acquisition where the last one functions to disappear are chewing and swallowing.
CONCLUSION. The transition from the adult EAM-AuMC into the infant AnBC, as a continuum in the individual biosphere, adds a contribution to the assessment of the retrogenesis in dementias from a multidimensional person-centered model.
